newsitem.title: MALI: Pre-poll mediation by Mali religious leaders fails.
newsitem.headline: Pre-poll mediation by Mali religious leaders fails.

text.p: Mali's religious leaders have called for peaceful polling in Sunday's rerun parliamentary election but have failed to bring President Alpha Oumar Konare and the boycotting radical opposition any closer.
Reverend Daniel Konate, spokesman for the Moslem and Christian clerics, told state television late on Wednesday that the two sides were deadlocked.
"We encountered a last-minute blockage on... holding a keenly anticipated roundtable," he said after 27 meetings.
He urged respect for Mali's traditions of tolerance, dialogue and consensus and appealed to all sides to assume their responsibilities and ensure the poll "takes place normally".
Mali was widely praised for its 1992 transition from Moussa Traore's dictatorship to a multi-party system.

An 18-party opposition alliance demanded that this year's second multi-party national elections be rescheduled after a chaotic April 13 parliamentary poll. It plans marches led by women militants to reinforce its boycott of Sunday's rerun.
The former French colony's constitutional court scrapped the April 13 parliamentary poll citing organisational chaos.
The opposition wanted the whole election timetable revised but Konare pressed ahead with a May 11 presidential election, won the backing of the court for that and then the election.
Konare's government has not formally banned protests but informed sources say that mixed patrols of police and gendarmes will take strict measures to ensure security on polling day.
Almost 600 candidates from Konare's Alliance for Democracy in Mali (ADEMA), 18 other parties and 13 independent lists will contest the 147 national assembly seats on Sunday.
